newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 6.

text.p: National MP John Baks said on Thursday he would vote against any deferment of the second round of tax cuts, throwing National's policy programme with NZ First into question. "Credibility could give way to pragmatism in what I consider a naked grab for power," Banks said on Thursday. A deal between the two could be in jeopardy if National cannot guarantee all its MPs will support important legislation like that needed to amend the tax cuts. Losing Banks' vote, or that of any other National MP, would take a National-NZ First coalition down to 60 votes in the 120-member house, not enough for a majority. Under
new parliamentary standing orders, the Speaker no longer has the casting vote. National would need one more vote to amend its legislation. Page 1.

The Reserve Bank hinted to exporters that a fall in the New Zealand dollar could be "fairly close at hand", but remained coy about when and by how much. Reserve Bank governor Don Brash spoke to an export summit in Wellington on Thursday and afterward told reporters the currency was near the top of its cycle. He said he was not attempting to signal to the markets. At the summit meeting of exporter groups, Brash tried to give

exporters the impression that a return to a more normal level for the dollar could be "fairly close at hand", according to sources who attended. Exporters' spokesman, Federated Farmers president Malcolm Bailey, said Brash had given exporters "comfort". Page 1.

Social Welfare Minister Peter Gresham on Thursday defended data matching by the Social Welfare Department against criticism by privacy commissioner Bruce Slane. Gresham said he was satisfied data matching was carried out legally and correctly and did not breach privacy. Page 2.

Labour has promised, if it becomes the government, to set up a full public inquiry into alleged false valuations for new homes. Labour leader Helen Clark and housing spokesman Paul Swain made the pledge on Thursday after meeting Fletcher Homes representatives. Fletcher Homes' managing director Bruce Nixon, corporate affairs manager David Lucas and their lawyer Geoffrey Palmer, gave Labour a 90-minute progress report on Fletcher's investigations into the allegations and subsequent complaints. Page 2.

Forestry company Carter Holt Harvey has confirmed a $300 million modernisation of its pulp and paper mill at Kinleith which will result in up to 150 redundancies. Chief executive John Faraci said one existing paper machine at the central North Island mill would be closed as a result of the modernisation, resulting in the redundancies. The upgrade would significantly reduce the cost of manufacturing at the mill, providing attractive returns for shareholders and customers, Faraci said. The main compenents of the modernisation were a new 100,000 tonne a year waste paper recycling operation, new pulp processing and drying machinery and a significant increase in
containerboard production. At the close of trading on Thursday, Carter Holt Harvey shares finished down four cents at $3.46 in heavy turnover. Page 14.

Sky City managing director Evan Davies criticised the government on Thursday for singling out the gaming industry as a tax source for purposes other than intended. He told the company's annual meeting in Auckland that the government justified levying the industry by citing costs of social consequences of gambling addiction. But he said a significant amount of the tax collected was not being put to that purpose.

He said Sky City intended lobbying the Internal Affairs Department over its review of the industry, particularly the view that some sectors of the industry should be relatively deregulated and open to more competition "while still maintaining an effective public monopoly" on provision of gaming entertainment in lotteries and horse racing. Page 14.
